# `internal/pki/testdata`

Fixtures for `golden_test.go`, the cross-validation test from spec section 10.

The test reproduces the certificate that `reconcile/engine.py` issues for
`nick-ipad` — using the identity from `config.hcl` — and asserts that what this
package produces is byte-identical to what `openssl` produced. `leaf.crt` is the
`openssl` side of that comparison, generated by the same two invocations
`engine.py` makes, so the reference is *measured* rather than described.

## These are not secrets

Every key here was generated fresh for the test suite. Nothing was copied from
the cluster, from Bitwarden, or from any other deployment. These keys sign
nothing outside this package's tests, no device trusts them, and they are
regenerable in a second from the commands below.

They are therefore safe to delete: `go test ./internal/pki/` will fail with a
"reading testdata/..." error until they are regenerated, and nothing else
breaks.

## Files

| File       | What it is                                                            |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ca.key`   | Throwaway ECDSA P-256 CA key, SEC1 PEM (`EC PRIVATE KEY`).             |
| `ca.crt`   | Self-signed CA certificate, `CN=homelab-golden-ca`, `keyCertSign,cRLSign`. |
| `leaf.key` | Throwaway RSA-2048 subject key, PKCS#8 PEM (`PRIVATE KEY`).            |
| `leaf.crt` | The reference leaf certificate, serial `0x2001`, issued by `ca.crt`.   |

`leaf.crt` carries exactly six extensions — `basicConstraints`, `keyUsage`,
`extendedKeyUsage`, `subjectKeyIdentifier`, `authorityKeyIdentifier`,
`subjectAltName` — and `golden_test.go` pins that set in `goldenExtensionOIDs`.
If a future `openssl` adds a seventh by default, the test fails loudly rather
than silently widening what it covers.

Two properties of `leaf.crt` are the whole point of the fixture:

- **Every DN value is a `UTF8String`** (ASN.1 tag `0x0c`), because `string_mask
  = utf8only` is set in `csr.cnf` exactly as `engine.py` sets it. Go's
  `asn1.Marshal` would emit `PrintableString` (`0x13`) for these same values,
  which is why `Attribute` carries an explicit `StringType`. Verify with
  `openssl asn1parse -in leaf.crt -i`.
- **`displayName` sits between `UID` and `GN`.** That interleaving is what
  `NamedSubject.Expand`'s canonical order cannot express, so the test uses the
  ordered `Subject` form.

## Regenerating

Generated with:

```
OpenSSL 3.5.7 9 Jun 2026 (Library: OpenSSL 3.5.7 9 Jun 2026)
```

Run from the repository root. Any `openssl` 3.x should reproduce equivalent
fixtures; the exact bytes differ because the keys, the serial of `ca.crt`, and
the validity dates are all fresh, but `golden_test.go` reads the validity dates
and the CA out of the fixtures rather than hardcoding them, so it does not care.

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/pki-golden && cd /tmp/pki-golden

# A CA to sign with. engine.py takes this as input; any CA with crlSign works.
openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout -out ca.key
openssl req -new -x509 -key ca.key -out ca.crt -days 7300 -subj "/CN=homelab-golden-ca" \
  -addext "basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE" \
  -addext "keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign"

# engine.py's _dn(): CN, UID, displayName (by OID), GN, SN, O -- utf8only.
cat > csr.cnf <<'EOF'
[req]
prompt = no
distinguished_name = dn
string_mask = utf8only
utf8 = yes
[dn]
CN = nick-ipad.ha.apps.somemissing.info
UID = nick
OID.2.16.840.1.113730.3.1.241 = Nick V
GN = Nick
SN = Venenga
O = homelab
EOF

# engine.py's _ext().
cat > ext.cnf <<'EOF'
[e]
basicConstraints = critical, CA:FALSE
keyUsage = critical, digitalSignature, keyEncipherment
extendedKeyUsage = clientAuth
subjectKeyIdentifier = hash
authorityKeyIdentifier = keyid, issuer
subjectAltName = @alt
[alt]
DNS.1 = nick-ipad.ha.apps.somemissing.info
email.1 = nick@venenga.com
email.2 = nijave@gmail.com
EOF

openssl genrsa -out leaf.key 2048
openssl req -new -key leaf.key -config csr.cnf -out leaf.csr
openssl x509 -req -in leaf.csr -CA ca.crt -CAkey ca.key \
  -set_serial $((0x2001)) -days 7305 -sha256 \
  -extfile ext.cnf -extensions e -out leaf.crt
```

Then copy the four files the test reads (`csr.cnf`, `ext.cnf`, and `leaf.csr` are
build inputs and are deliberately not committed):

```bash
cp ca.crt ca.key leaf.key leaf.crt <repo>/internal/pki/testdata/
```

Note that `authorityKeyIdentifier = keyid, issuer` resolves to *keyid only* in
`leaf.crt`. `openssl`'s `issuer` flag, without `always`, emits the issuer name
and serial only when `keyid` cannot be resolved, and `ca.crt` carries a
`subjectKeyIdentifier` for it to copy. That is why `golden_test.go` can compare
`AuthorityKeyId` directly against what `crypto/x509` synthesizes.
